title: English Practice Quiz 0943
description: A ten-question English practice quiz covering grammar, vocabulary and practical communication.

questions.question: When answering a business call, you should begin with ___.
options: a polite greeting and your organisation or name
a request for the caller's password
questions.explanation: A greeting identifies the person or organisation and sets a professional tone.

questions.question: If you need to place a caller on hold, you should ___.
questions.explanation: Asking first is courteous and gives the caller a choice.

questions.question: A caller's message should include the caller's name and ___.
options: a contact number and reason for calling
questions.explanation: These details help the intended recipient return the call.

questions.question: If a call is difficult to hear, you can say ___.
questions.explanation: This politely asks the caller to repeat the information.

questions.question: A call transfer should ideally be made after ___.
options: explaining who will take the call
asking the caller to dial random numbers
questions.explanation: A brief explanation makes the transfer smoother.

questions.question: When taking an important phone message, it is useful to ___.
options: repeat key details to confirm accuracy
change the message to sound better

questions.question: If the intended person is unavailable, offer to ___.
options: take a message or suggest an appropriate time to call
share their private schedule with everyone
promise an immediate response without checking
questions.explanation: Offering a message or callback option is helpful and respectful.

questions.question: A voicemail greeting should be ___.
questions.explanation: A concise greeting tells callers whose mailbox they reached and what to do.

questions.question: The phrase 'May I know who is calling?' is used to ask for the caller's ___.
questions.explanation: It is a polite way to ask who is on the line.

questions.question: Before ending a service call, it is useful to ___.
options: confirm whether the caller needs anything else
hang up while they are speaking
questions.explanation: A final check helps ensure the caller's concern has been addressed.
